Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Tafsir of Surat al-Ahzab

It is Madani, according to the consensus of all.

﴿O Prophet, fear Allah.﴾ Regarding this there are several opinions. The first: (i.e.) persist in taqwa (God-consciousness), like a man who says to another who is standing, "Stand here," meaning: remain standing. The second opinion: the address is to the Messenger, and what is meant is his community (ummah).

It has also been said regarding the verse, "fear Allah," that it means: increase your means of taqwa. Taqwa is: acting in obedience to Allah, hoping for the mercy of Allah, upon a light from Allah, and abstaining from disobedience to Allah, fearing the punishment of Allah, upon a light from Allah. And in the verse there is a fourth opinion, which is what has been narrated: that Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Abu al-A'war al-Sulami came to Madinah during the period of the truce and asked the Messenger of Allah for objectionable things; the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims were then prompted to kill them, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah.﴾ That is: do not break the covenant that is between you and them. This was related by al-Dahhak.

As for His saying: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites.﴾ That is: the disbelievers from the people of Makkah, and the hypocrites from the people of Madinah.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ That is: Knowing of His creation before He created them, Wise in what He has arranged for them.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord﴾, i.e., from the Qur'an.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾, i.e., Acquainted with your deeds.

"His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And put your trust in God﴾, that is: have confidence in God.

And His saying: ﴿And God suffices as a Trustee﴾, that is: God suffices as a Guardian for you. It is also said: God suffices as a Guarantor who provides for you."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 4:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾. There are several opinions regarding this verse.

The first: what al-Suddi and others mentioned, that a man was called Jamil ibn Mu'ammar, though the more correct name is Abu Mu'ammar Jamil ibn Asad. The people of the Jahiliyyah (Pre-Islamic Age of Ignorance) used to call him "the one with two hearts" because of the intensity of his intelligence and sharpness. When Allah Exalted defeated the polytheists on the Day of Badr, and he was with them, he also fled. Abu Sufyan met him with one of his sandals on his foot and the other held in his hand. He said to him: "What is the matter with the people?" He said: "They have been defeated." He said: "What is the matter with your sandal in your hand?" He said: "I did not know except that it was on my foot." So they realised that he had only one heart, and Allah Exalted revealed this verse.

The second opinion: the hypocrites used to say: "Muhammad has two hearts: one with you and one with his companions." So Allah Exalted revealed this verse and informed that he has only one heart.

The third opinion: what has been related from al-Hasan al-Basri, that he said: "One of them would say: 'I have a self that commands me to good and a self that commands me to evil.' So Allah Exalted revealed this verse and informed that no one has except one self and one heart. Commanding to good comes by the inspiration of Allah, and commanding to evil comes by the inspiration of Satan."

The fourth opinion: ﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾, meaning: Allah has not made for any man two parents. Al-Shafi'i argued with this in the issue of the qa'if (physiognomer who determines lineage by resemblance), and said: "Because Zayd ibn Harithah was attributed to the Prophet by sonship, Allah Exalted said: ﴿Allah has not made for any man﴾ two parents, meaning: he is the son of Harithah, and not the son of the Prophet."

His saying: ﴿Nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by zihar your mothers﴾. Zihar is that a man says to his wife: "You are to me like the back of my mother." They used to count it as a divorce. If it is said: "How is this reconciled with what preceded?" The answer: its meaning is that the matter is not as you claim, of a man having two hearts or two parents, nor as you claim, that the woman becomes like a mother through zihar. As for the meaning and ruling of zihar, we shall mention it in Surah al-Mujadila.

His saying: ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾. In this verse is the abrogation of adoption (tabanni). In the Jahiliyyah a man would adopt another man and make him a son to himself like a son born to him, and upon this the Messenger of Allah adopted Zayd ibn Harithah, so Allah abrogated that.

His saying: ﴿That is your saying by your mouths﴾, meaning: it is a saying that has no reality.

His saying: ﴿And Allah says the truth﴾, meaning: His saying is the truth in forbidding adoption.

His saying: ﴿And He guides to the way﴾, meaning: He guides to the path of truth.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers﴾. It has been established, through the transmission of Musa ibn Uqba, from Salim, from Ibn Umar, that he said: "We would not call Zayd ibn Haritha anything but Zayd ibn Muhammad until Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers﴾."

The Shaykh, the Imam, said: Mukki ibn Abd al-Razzaq informed us of this, Abu al-Haytham informed us, al-Farabri informed us, al-Bukhari informed us, Mu'alla ibn Asad informed us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar, from Musa ibn Uqba... the hadith.

As for His saying: ﴿That is more just in the sight of Allah﴾, meaning: more equitable in the sight of Allah.

As for His saying: ﴿But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion﴾, meaning: name them with the names of your brothers in religion, such as Abd Allah, Abd al-Karim, Abd al-Rahman, Abd al-Aziz, and the like.

As for His saying: ﴿and your clients﴾: this is the saying of a man to another man: "I am your brother and your client (mawla)," or he says: "I am your brother and your guardian (wali)." It is also said: "Your brothers in religion" refers to those who were originally free, and "your clients" refers to those who were freed. It is also said: "your clients" refers to one who embraced Islam at your hands.

As for His saying: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you have erred in﴾: the error in this is that a person says to another, "O son of so-and-so," while he thinks he is his son, and then it becomes clear that he is not his son.

A second opinion: the error here is what they did before the prohibition, and the deliberate act is what they did after the prohibition.

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: Concealing and Compassionate.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 6:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾, meaning: more so than some of them are to others.

It has been established that the Prophet said: "I am closer to every believing man and woman than his own self. Whoever leaves behind wealth, it goes to his heirs; whoever leaves behind debt or dependants, then it is for me (to take care of)."

There is another view regarding the verse, which is that its meaning is: when the Messenger calls a person to something, and his own self calls him to something else, he follows the Messenger and does not follow the self. The third view is what has been narrated: that the Prophet used to go out to jihad, and some people would say, "O Messenger of Allah, we will go and seek permission from our fathers and our mothers," so God the Exalted revealed this verse.

As for His saying: ﴿and his wives are their mothers﴾, meaning: in terms of prohibition (of marriage) specifically, not in terms of looking at them and entering upon them. In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy it reads: "and his wives are their mothers, and he is a father to them."

Scholars differed regarding the woman from whom the Prophet separated before his death, in three ways: one view is that she is also forbidden; the other view is that she is not forbidden; and the third view is that if he had consummated the marriage with her, she is forbidden, but if he had not consummated it with her, she is not forbidden.

Scholars also differed as to whether they (the wives) are the mothers of the believing women, with two views: one view is that they are the mothers of the believing women just as they are the mothers of the believers; the other view is that they are the mothers of the men but not of the women. It is narrated that a woman said to Aisha, "O mother," and she said, "I am the mother of your men, not of your women."

As for the brothers of the Prophet's wives, they are not the maternal uncles of the believers, and likewise the sisters of the Prophet's wives are not the maternal aunts of the believers.

It is narrated that Asma' bint Abi Bakr was married to al-Zubayr, and the Companions said, "Al-Zubayr has the sister of the Mother of the Believers (as a wife)," and they did not say, "He has the maternal aunt of the believers (as a wife)."

His saying: ﴿and blood relatives are closer to one another in the Book of Allah﴾, meaning: some of them are closer to others in inheritance according to the judgment of God. They used to inherit from one another through emigration, and God the Exalted abrogated that in favour of inheritance by kinship. It is narrated that the Prophet established brotherhood between the Emigrants and the Helpers, and he used to inherit from one another, and then that was abrogated.

His saying: ﴿from among the believers and the emigrants﴾ is evidence that believers do not inherit from disbelievers, and disbelievers do not inherit from believers.

His saying: ﴿and the emigrants﴾ is evidence that an emigrant does not inherit from non-emigrants, nor does a non-emigrant inherit from an emigrant.

His saying: ﴿except that you do to your allies a kindness﴾ has two interpretations: the first is: except that you make a bequest to non-relatives who are of your religion; the real meaning is that their inheritance was abrogated, while the permissibility of bequest remained. The second view is that the intended meaning of the verse is bequest to disbelievers, so the meaning according to this is: disbelievers do not inherit from Muslims, but if one bequeaths to them, it is permissible.

His saying: ﴿That was written in the Book, inscribed﴾, meaning: in the Preserved Tablet; it is also said: in the Qur'an and the rest of the books of God.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 7:

And His saying: ﴿And [remember] when We took from the prophets their covenant﴾. Al-Mithaq (the covenant) is the binding pledge, and the strongest form of pledge is swearing an oath by Allah.

And His saying: ﴿and from you, and from Noah﴾. Scholars have differed concerning the placement of the Prophet (ﷺ). One of the two opinions is what Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "I am the first of the prophets in creation and the last of them in being sent."

And from Qatadah, who said: "He began with him in creation and concluded with him in being sent." The second opinion is that the conjunction "wa" (and) indicates togetherness and does not require any precedence or sequence. So it is as if He said: "We took the covenant of these prophets," and these were singled out because they were the bearers of the sacred laws (ashab al-shara'i), namely: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus [son of Mary], and Muhammad. As for the meaning of al-mithaq, the people of tafsir said: He took from them a pledge that they would worship Allah, call people to the worship of Allah, confirm one another, and give sincere advice to the people. It is also said: He took from Noah a pledge to give glad tidings of Abraham, and from Abraham a pledge to give glad tidings of Moses, [and from Moses a pledge to give glad tidings of Jesus], and so on until Muhammad.

And His saying: ﴿And We took from them a firm covenant﴾. We have explained this before.

It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that he said: The offspring of Adam were taken from the loins of Adam, and the prophets were among them like lamps shining, and He took the covenant from them. And from some of them: The spirits were created before the bodies, and the covenant was taken from the spirits.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 8:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness﴾, meaning: that He may question the prophets about their conveying of the message. If someone says: what is the wisdom in questioning them about conveying the message? The answer: the wisdom in that is to rebuke those to whom they were sent. On this same meaning is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when Allah says, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'"﴾.

It is also said: "That He may question the truthful" about their deeds done for Allah. And it is said: "That He may question the truthful with their mouths about their truthfulness in their hearts."

As for His saying, ﴿And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment﴾, the first statement has been completed, and this is the beginning of a new statement, and its meaning is known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 9:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you﴾. That is: the bounty (minnah) of Allah upon you.

And His statement: ﴿When there came to you soldiers﴾. What is meant by "soldiers" (junud) is the confederates (al-Ahzab) who banded together against the Messenger of Allah. They were: the Quraysh, led by Abu Sufyan; the Asad, led by Tulayha ibn Khuwaylid; and the Ghatafan, led by Uyayna ibn Hisn. Their number reached twelve thousand, and the leader of the group was Abu Sufyan. They intended to uproot the Prophet and his Companions. The Jews of Banu Qurayza joined them and were part of their affair, and they broke the covenant that had been between them and the Prophet, in a lengthy account. When the Prophet learned of their affair, he dug the trench (khandaq) around Medina, and this is the Battle of the Trench (Ghazwat al-Khandaq) and the Gathering of the Confederates (Jam' al-Ahzab).

And His statement: ﴿So We sent upon them a wind﴾. In the interpretation: Allah, exalted is He, sent upon them the east wind (rih al-Saba), until it routed them. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I was helped by the Sabā, and 'Ad was destroyed by the Dabur." The wind would uproot their tents, overturn their cooking pots, and throw dust into their faces, and their horses collided with one another; so they fled and departed, and Allah sufficed them in their affair.

And His statement: ﴿And soldiers you did not see﴾. That is: the angels.

And His statement: ﴿And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing﴾. The meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 10:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you﴾. In the exegesis: those who came from above them were Asad and Ghatafan.

And His words: ﴿and from below you﴾ are the Quraysh and Kinanah. It is also said: those who came from above them were Qurayzah, and from below you were the Quraysh and Ghatafan.

And His words: ﴿and when the eyes swerved﴾, meaning the eyes became fixed in terror. In Arabic, the meaning of "zaaghat" (swerved) is "maalat" (inclined), so it is as if they inclined while staring fixedly. This is from the dread and fear.

And His words: ﴿and the hearts reached the throats﴾, meaning they moved from their places and rose up. Qatadah said: "Had they found a way out, they would have come out through the throats, but they were constricted." The more correct view regarding the meaning is that this is by way of metaphor (tamthil). The Arabs say: "The heart of so-and-so reached his throat," meaning from terror and fear. The "hanjarah" (throat, the windpipe) is the letter-point of the gullet (hulqum), and it is an expression for the intensity of alarm.

And His words: ﴿and you thought thoughts about Allah﴾, meaning: the alif was added to match the endings (awakhir) of the verses in the surah.

The poet said:

(Cease, O blamer, your reproach and rebuke... and my saying, if I am right, then I have been right)

That is: cease, O my blamer, reproach and rebuke.

"Allah the Exalted said: ﴿There the believers were tested﴾. Hunālika (هنالك) in the language is for the distant, hunā (هنا) for the near, and hunāka (هناك) for the intermediate. The meaning of hunālika is 'hā hunā,' i.e., 'at that time the believers were tested.'

And His saying: ﴿and they were shaken with a severe shaking﴾, i.e., they were moved with a violent movement. It is also read zalzālan (زلزالا) with a fatḥah on the zāy, but the more well-known reading is with a kasrah on the zāy, zilzālan (زلزالا), and this is the more correct in Arabic.

Among the well-known reports: a man said to Ḥudhayfah (raḍiya Allāh ʿanhu): 'You saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and were in his company. By Allah, if we had seen him, we would have carried him on our necks.' Ḥudhayfah said: 'I inform you, O man, that we were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Battle of the Trench (al-Khandaq), and hardship, hunger and fear reached us to the extent that Allah alone knows. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Who among you will go and bring news of the people, and Allah will make him my companion in Paradise?" None of us answered him because of the severity of the matter. Then he said a second time, and none of us answered him. Then he said a third time, and none of us answered him. He said: "O Ḥudhayfah!" I could not refrain from answering, so I came to him. He said: "Go and bring me news of the people, and do not do anything until you come back to me." He called me, so I went and brought him news of the people, in a story . . ."

Ḥudhayfah only intended by this report that a person should not wish for something he has not experienced, for perhaps he would not be patient under trial if he encountered it."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 12:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion."﴾ They differed concerning the speaker of this statement. Some said: it was Aws ibn Qayzi. Others said: it was Abdullah ibn Ubayy. And others said: it was Mu'attib ibn Qushayr. As for the promise which they called "delusion," it is what has been narrated: "When the Prophet ordered the digging of the trench (khandaq), he divided the digging among his companions, and Salman was assigned together with the Banu Hashim. He began to dig, and reached a rock he could not break. The Messenger of Allah took the pickaxe from his hand and struck the rock one blow, and it lit up like a shining star. Then he did the same a second and a third time. Salman said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have seen something wondrous!' The Messenger of Allah said: 'And did you see it?' He said: 'Yes. In the first blow I saw the palaces of Yemen, in the second blow the White Cities, that is, the palace of Kisra, and in the third blow I saw the palaces of Syria.' So he said: 'Allah will surely open them for my community.' This spread among the people. When matters reached the state they reached, these people said: 'Muhammad promises us the kingdoms of Kisra and Caesar, while one of us cannot even step away from his saddle to relieve himself. This is nothing but delusion.' So Allah the Most High revealed the verse we have mentioned."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when a faction of them said, "O people of Yathrib"﴾ refers to Medina. It is said: Yathrib is a place, and Medina is part of it. Hassan ibn Thabit (Hassan ibn Thabit) said in verse:

("I shall send to her every year a poem, and I shall sit, protected, honored in Yathrib.")

And in some reports: "The Prophet forbade that Medina be called Yathrib, and said: 'It is Taba (Taba).'" It seems that peace and blessings be upon him disliked this term, because it derives from tathrib (reproach).

And His saying: ﴿There is no place for you to stay﴾. It was also read "la muqama lakum" with a raised mim. So His saying ﴿there is no place for you to stay﴾ means: there is no residence (iqamah) for you. And His saying ﴿la muqama lakum﴾ with a fatha on the mim means: there is no dwelling (manzil) for you.

And His saying: ﴿So return﴾, meaning: turn back from following Muhammad, and take your security from the polytheists.

And His saying: ﴿And a party of them asked permission of the Prophet﴾. These were the Banu Salamah and the Banu Haritha, and it is said: others as well.

And His saying: ﴿They say, "Indeed our houses are exposed (awrah)"﴾, meaning: having a weakness (dhat awrah). It is said: exposed, easy for thieves to enter. It is also said: "Indeed our houses are awrah" means: constricted. Al-Farra' said: awrah means with weak walls, not secure. In the irregular reading, "awrah" is read with a fatha on the ayn and a kasra on the waw, and the meaning returns to what we have explained.

And His saying: ﴿And they are not exposed (awrah)﴾, meaning: they are lying in their claim, and they only want to flee. This is the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They only intend to flee﴾. And they cited for the word awrah:

("Until, when it cast a hand upon a disbeliever, and the darkness of the frontiers' gaps (awrat) covered it.")

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 14:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if they had been entered upon from all its sides﴾, meaning: from its surrounding areas.

And His saying: ﴿Then they were asked for fitnah﴾, meaning: shirk (associating partners with God). It is also said: fighting out of tribal partisanship (ʿaṣabiyyah).

And His saying: ﴿They would have given it﴾, with the long vowel (ālīn? no: "ātūhā" with a madd), and it was recited as "atawhā" (without the long vowel). So His saying "ātawhā" with the madd means: they would have given it (aʿṭawhā); and His saying "atawhā" means: they would have aimed for it (qaṣadūhā).

And His saying: ﴿And they would not have delayed in it except briefly﴾, meaning: they would not have reckoned on it except briefly, and they would have given what was demanded of them, willingly and with their own souls.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they had already covenanted with Allah before, that they would not turn their backs﴾. Al-adbar (the backs) is the plural of al-dubur, meaning: they would not flee in defeat.

Muqatil and others mentioned that this refers to those who pledged allegiance with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of al-'Aqabah. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, set a condition for your Lord." He said: "That you worship Him and associate nothing with Him." They said: "Set a condition for yourself." He said: "That you protect me as you protect yourselves and your children." The number of those who pledged allegiance on the night of al-'Aqabah was [seventy] men, and the first to pledge was Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan. This view is not sound, because the Companions of al-'Aqabah had no doubters among them, nor anyone who would say such a thing. Rather, the verse concerns a people who covenanted that they would fight and not flee until they were killed, and they broke the covenant.

And His saying: ﴿And the covenant of Allah will be questioned﴾, meaning: it will be questioned about it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 16:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing﴾. It means: the appointed term will overtake you at its appointed time.

And His statement: ﴿And then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little﴾. Its meaning: until the end of your appointed terms. In some reports it is related that a man was defeated in some battle, and he was blamed for that, and this verse was recited to him: ﴿Say: Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing; and then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little﴾. He said: "That little is what I seek."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: "Who is it that can protect you from Allah?"﴾ That is: who can grant you refuge and prevent you (from Him)?

And His saying: ﴿if He intends for you harm﴾ That is: defeat, and the victory of your enemy over you.

And His saying: ﴿or intends for you mercy﴾ That is: good and support.

And His saying: ﴿nor will they find for themselves other than Allah any ally or any helper﴾ That is: a near one who benefits them, and a helper who protects them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 18:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah already knows those among you who hinder (al-mu'awwiqin)﴾. It is said: "‘awwaqahu," "a'taqahu," and "‘awwaqahu" mean he diverted him from what he intended. It is also said: "al-mu'awwiqin minkum" means "al-muthabbitin minkum," i.e., those among you who discourage (others).

And His words: ﴿and those who say to their brothers, "Come here to us!"﴾, i.e., return to us.

And His words: ﴿and they do not come to battle except a little﴾, i.e., they do not fight except a little, out of showing off and seeking reputation, without seeking reward. The verse was revealed concerning a group of the hypocrites who said, when the armies surrounded the Muslims: "Muhammad and his people are a morsel to be eaten! By Allah, if Muhammad and his companions were meat, Abu Sufyan and his party would devour them," i.e., swallow them up. They used to say to the Ansar, the companions of Muhammad: "Leave Muhammad, for Muhammad intends to kill you all."

Al-Kalbi said concerning His words ﴿except a little﴾: it means, except throwing stones.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 33, verse 19:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Stingy towards you﴾, meaning: stingy in giving help and support in fighting. Qatadah said: stingy at the time of the spoils of war. So it is as if God, the Exalted, said: they are the best of people at the time of fighting, and the most stingy of people at the time of the spoils.

And His saying: ﴿When fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like those of one who is overcome by death﴾. The one who is overcome by death has lost his reason and his gaze becomes fixed, and this is the dying person who has come near to death.

And His saying: ﴿But when fear departs, they lash at you with sharp tongues﴾. Al-Farra' said: they fall upon you with eloquent, sharp tongues. It is related from some of them: they lash at you with sharp tongues, meaning: at the time of seeking spoils and in vain disputation. It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Obscenity (al-badha') and eloquence (al-bayan) are two branches of hypocrisy, and modesty (al-haya') and reticence (al-'iyy) are two branches of faith."

The Arabs say: "a khatib (orator) who is musallaq (fluent) and sallaq," when he is eloquent in speech. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "they lash at you" means they slander you and attack you with defamation and backbiting. al-A'sha said:

(Among them are fertility, generosity and valour, and among them is the eloquent orator who lashes out.)

And His saying: ﴿Stingy towards good﴾ — we have already explained that this refers to the time of the spoils.

And in the report: "The Prophet (ﷺ) said to the Ansar: 'Indeed you are many at the time of terror and few at the time of greed'", meaning: you gather at the time of fighting and scatter at the time of taking wealth. As for the description of the hypocrites, it is the opposite of this: they were cowardly at the time of fighting and stingy at the time of wealth.

And His saying: ﴿Those have not believed, so God has nullified their deeds﴾, meaning: God has rendered their deeds void.

And His saying: ﴿And that is easy for God﴾, meaning: simple.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 20:

The Almighty's words: ﴿They think the confederates have not withdrawn﴾, meaning: out of cowardice and fear.

And His words: ﴿And if the confederates should come [again]﴾, meaning: they would return after having gone away.

And His words: ﴿They would wish that they were in the desert among the Bedouins﴾. Al-badun (the desert dwellers) are the opposite of those who are present; they are the ones who live in the desert (al-badiyah). His words ﴿among the Bedouins﴾ mean: with the Bedouins (al-A'rab).

And His words: ﴿They ask about your news﴾, meaning: about your reports. The meaning of their asking about the reports is that victory was for the polytheists, or for Muhammad and his companions.

And His words: ﴿And had they been among you, they would not have fought except a little﴾, meaning: [only] as an excuse (ta'dhir). The meaning of ta'dhir is that they would fight something slight by which they could establish their excuse, so they would say, "We have fought."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 21:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example﴾, i.e., an excellent model (qudwah hasanah). Al-ta'assi (imitation, following the example) is al-iqtida' (emulation). He mentioned the "example" here so that they would be helped (and stand firm) and endure what befalls them, just as the Messenger of Allah did. His front tooth (ruba'iyyah) was broken on the Day of Uhud, his forehead was wounded, the helmet was broken upon his head, and his uncle was killed, yet he did not slacken in the matter of Allah, and he endured all of that.

His saying: ﴿for whoever hopes for Allah and the Last Day﴾, i.e., hopes for the reward of Allah. It has also been said: for whoever fears Allah and the Last Day, for raja' (hope) can carry the meaning of khashyah (fear), and it can also carry the meaning of tama' (desire).

His saying: ﴿and remembers Allah often﴾, i.e., in all circumstances, in ease and in hardship.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 22:

The Most High's saying: ﴿When the believers saw the confederates, they said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth."﴾ Qatadah said: The meaning of this verse refers back to the Most High's saying in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise without there having come to you the like of what came to those who passed away before you? Adversity and hardship touched them, and they were shaken, until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?"﴾ This verse contains the meaning that the believers would encounter and face such trials. So when they saw that on the Day of the Trench, they said: "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us."

And it is related from some of them that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his Companions: "Indeed, the polytheists are marching toward you, and they will descend upon you in ten [days]," or as he said. So when the believers saw the confederates, [they said: "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us"], and they had marched toward them. ﴿And it only increased them in faith and submission.﴾ That is: in affirmation of Allah, and in submission to the command of Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 23:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with Allah﴾. That is: they stood by what they had covenanted with Allah. It is also said: they stood firmly to the matter, in fulfilment and truthfulness.

And His saying: ﴿So among them is one who has fulfilled his vow﴾. The word nahb (vow) occurs with many meanings, and the most preferred meaning here is that it means the covenant (ʿahd). So the meaning of the verse is: he completed the covenant and stood by it. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: that is, he upheld fulfilment and truthfulness.

Ibn Qutaybah said: the nahb is the nadhr (vow), and the meaning of "fulfilled his vow" here is: he was killed in the way of Allah. As if the people, by their acceptance of faith, vowed to die in a manner that pleases Allah, so whoever was killed in the way of Allah had fulfilled his vow.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: the verse concerns those who were martyred on the day of Uhud, namely Hamzah (may Allah be pleased with him) and those martyred with him.

It is also established by the narration of Yazid ibn Harun, from Humayd, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), that his uncle al-Nadr ibn Anas had been absent from Badr. He said: "I was absent from the first expedition that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) undertook. If Allah shows me fighting against the polytheists, Allah will surely see what I do." Then, on the day of Uhud, when the Muslims were routed, al-Nadr ibn Anas saw this and said: "O Allah, I apologise to You for what these people have done"—meaning the Muslims—"and I disown what these people have done"—meaning the polytheists. Then he advanced against the faces of the disbelievers and met Saʿd ibn Muʿadh beyond Uhud. Saʿd said to him: "I am with you." Saʿd said: "I was not able to do what he did." He was found with more than eighty wounds from sword blows, spear thrusts and arrow shots. In another narration: "None could recognise him except his sister by his molars." Anas said: "It was concerning him and those who were martyred that this was revealed: ﴿So among them is one who has fulfilled his vow, and among them is one who awaits﴾."

That is: among the believers there remained, after those who were martyred, those who await one of two things: either martyrdom in the way of Allah or victory.

They also recited poetry about the nahb:

(He fulfilled the vow of life, and every living being, when called to his death, responds.)

It is also well known that the nahb means a great peril. Jarir said about the nahb:

(At Takhfa we fought the kings, and we left, on the evening of Bisṭām, those who ran upon a nahb.)

That is: upon a great peril.

His saying: ﴿And they did not change in the least﴾. That is: they did not abandon what they had accepted and covenanted to.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 24:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness﴾, i.e., the reward of their truthfulness, and their truthfulness is their fulfilment of the covenant.

And His saying: ﴿and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or accept their repentance﴾, meaning He guides them to faith.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, i.e., Concealing (sattar) and Compassionate ('atuf).

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 33, verse 25:

God's words: ﴿And God turned back those who disbelieved in their rage﴾, meaning: He repelled them, and they did not gain satisfaction against Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions, although they had intended to uproot them entirely.

And His words: ﴿they did not attain﴾, meaning: they did not achieve what they had intended.

And His words: ﴿[good]. And God sufficed the believers in fighting﴾, meaning: by the wind that He sent against them. In some rare narrations from Ibn 'Abbas: "And God sufficed the believers in fighting," meaning: for 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him), who on that day killed 'Amr ibn 'Abd Wudd, who was one of the great leaders of the disbelievers. 'Amr ibn 'Abd Wudd struck him on his head with a blow that day. When he struck him, Ibn Muljam's blow fell on the place of 'Amr ibn 'Abd Wudd's blow, and so he perished from that (may God be pleased with him).

And His words: ﴿And God is ever Powerful, Mighty﴾, meaning: powerful in His dominion, mighty in His retribution.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 33, verse 26:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Book who supported them﴾, i.e., those of the People of the Book who aided them (the confederates). They were the Banu Qurayzah, who were during the time of the Prophet, and their chief was Ka'b ibn Asad. As for the Banu al-Nadir, their chief was Huyayy ibn Akhtab. When the Messenger of Allah expelled the Banu al-Nadir to Syria, Huyayy ibn Akhtab went to the Quraysh and sought their support (istansarahum), gathered the confederate tribes (al-Ahzab), and brought them to fight the Prophet. Then he came to Qurayzah and incited them to break the covenant, in a long story. He also made a pact with them that if the polytheists returned without achieving victory, he would enter their fortress with them so that he would suffer what they suffered. When the polytheists were defeated, he entered their fortress with them. As for Qurayzah, they broke the covenant and aimed to fight the Prophet along with the confederates, in a story mentioned in the books of Maghazi (military expeditions).

His saying: ﴿from their fortresses﴾, i.e., from their strongholds. From this comes the word sayasi (horns), i.e., the horns of cattle, because they defend themselves with them.

His saying: ﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾, i.e., fear.

His saying: ﴿a group you killed﴾. The Messenger of Allah killed four hundred and fifty of Qurayzah, and in another narration six hundred, and among them were Huyayy ibn Akhtab and their leaders. They used to say: "This is a slaughter that Allah prescribed for the Children of Israel."

His saying: ﴿and you took captive a group﴾. He took seven hundred and fifty of them captive, and in another narration seven hundred.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 27:

﴿And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth﴾. That is: He made you gain booty (aghnamakum).

As for His saying: ﴿And land which you had not trodden﴾, the most evident of the opinions is that it is Khaybar. ʿIkrimah said: it is everything that God, exalted is He, has conquered and will conquer of the lands of the polytheists until the Day of Resurrection. It is also reported from some of them that it refers to Persia and Byzantium.

As for His saying: ﴿And God is over all things capable﴾, that is: Capable (qadiran).

As for the story of the killing of Qurayza, it is as related: that the Prophet, when he returned from the Trench to his house and put down his weapons (laamatahu), that is, his armour, and washed himself, Jibril, peace be upon him, came upon a horse and called him. When he came out of his house, he said: "Do you lay down your weapons while the angels have not laid down their weapons? The dust was on his face and the face of his horse." He said: "O Jibril, where to?" He said: "To Qurayza." So the Prophet went out, and his companions went out to Qurayza, and he called out to his companions: "None of you should pray ʿAsr except in [the land of the Banu] Qurayza." So they did not pray until the sun had set; some of them prayed ʿAsr, and some did not pray until they arrived, and he did not rebuke either of the two groups. He besieged them for twenty-one nights, and they came down under the judgment of Saʿd ibn Muʿadh. They had been his allies in the Jahiliyyah. Saʿd ibn Muʿadh was the chief of the Aws, and Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah was the chief of the Khazraj. When they came down under his judgment, Saʿd was ill in Medina, in his house, from an arrow that had struck his arm-artery (akhal) on the day of the Trench, and the blood would not stop. So he called upon God, exalted is He, and said: "O God, let me live until You show me what will gladden my eye regarding Qurayza." Then the blood stopped.

When they came down under his judgment, the Messenger of God summoned him, and he came on a grey donkey, surrounded by his people, who kept saying to him: "Your allies and your clients." Saʿd said: "The time has come for Saʿd that he should not fear in God the blame of any blamer." When he came to the Prophet, peace be upon him said to the Ansar: "Rise up for your chief." Then he judged that the fighting men should be killed, the children (dhurriyyah) taken captive, and the property divided. The Prophet said to him: "You have judged by the judgment of the King." It is also related that he said: "I have judged by the judgment of God from above His Throne." Then he carried out with them what he had judged. Then Saʿd, when they were killed, said: "O God, if You have left some war between Your Messenger and Quraysh, then let me live for it; and if You have ended the war between Your Messenger and Quraysh, then take me to You." His wound burst at that moment, and they were not alerted except by the blood flowing toward them. He died from that, may God be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 28:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment…﴾ to the end of the verse. The exegetes (al-mufassirun) said: The occasion of the revelation of the verse was that the wives of the Prophet asked him for some of worldly things, and he did not have them, and they asked him for an increase in maintenance (nafaqa), and they harmed him by their rivalry with one another. So Allah the Exalted revealed the verse of choice (ayat al-takhyir).

Al-Naqqash, in his tafsir, related from al-Dahhak that Zaynab bint Jahsh asked him for a garment of musammar (a striped striped cloak, a striped burd); Maymunah asked him for a Yemeni robe (hullah); Umm Habibah asked him for a garment of green cloths; Juwayriyah asked him for a headcloth (mi'jar); and it is related from some of them that she asked him for a qatifah (a thick cloak), and he had none of that. It is also related that they said: "If we were with someone other than him, we would have jewelry and garments." So Allah the Exalted revealed the verse of choice. It is established that the Prophet made a vow (ila') regarding them for a month and withdrew in an upper room, in a lengthy account.

In some narrations from Ibn 'Abbas, the Prophet was in the house of Hafsah and they quarrelled. The Messenger of Allah said to her: "Shall I make between me and you a man? Do you want your father?" She said: "Yes." So he called 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. When he entered, the Prophet said to Hafsah: "Speak."

Hafsah said: "O Messenger of Allah, speak, and say only what is true." 'Umar raised his hand and struck her face, and said: "O enemy of herself, do you say this to the Messenger of Allah?" Then the Messenger of Allah made a vow regarding them for a month and withdrew, and Allah the Exalted revealed the verse of choice. When Allah revealed the verse of choice, he began with 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.

This has been established by the narration of al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from 'A'ishah, that the Prophet began with her when Allah the Exalted revealed the verse of choice. 'A'ishah said: "He came to me and said: 'O 'A'ishah, I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm for you in not hurrying until you consult your two parents.' He knew that my parents would not order me to part from him. Then he recited the verse to me. I said: 'Am I to consult my parents about this? Indeed, I choose Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode.' Then he presented that to the rest of his wives, and they said the same." This report was related by al-Bukhari from Abu al-Yaman, from Shu'ayb, from al-Zuhri, and the chain is as we have explained before.

As for his wives whom he gave the choice, they were nine: five of them were Qurashi women: 'A'ishah bint Abi Bakr, Hafsah bint 'Umar, Umm Salamah bint Umayyah, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, and Sawdah bint Zam'ah. As for the non-Qurashi: Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, Safiyyah bint Huyayy al-Khaybariyyah, Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, and Juwayriyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyyah.

The exegetes said: When they chose him, Allah the Exalted thanked them for that, and He forbade the Prophet from marrying others besides them or exchanging them, and this is in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry] women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty impresses you﴾. We will mention the ruling on that later.

The scholars differed concerning this choice: was it a divorce (talaq)? It was only that he gave them a choice: if they chose the world, he would separate from them without divorce, and if they chose him, he would keep them. A group of scholars held that this choice was a divorce, so it was as if he had given them the choice and, had they chosen themselves, it would have been a divorce.

The Companions differed concerning a man who says to his wife: "Choose." And she says: "I have chosen myself." 'Umar held that if she chose her husband, it counts as nothing, and if she chose herself, it is one revocable divorce, and the husband has the greater right to take her back.

'Ali said: If she chooses her husband, it is one divorce, and the husband has the greater right to take her back; and if she chooses herself, it is one irrevocable divorce (bd'ina), and the husband does not have the right to take her back. He also held that if she chooses her husband, it is one revocable divorce, and if she chooses herself, it is three. It has been said other than this. These three opinions are the well-known ones, and a group of scholars adopted each of these opinions. The evidence that if she chooses her husband it is not a divorce is that 'A'ishah said: "The Messenger of Allah gave us the choice, and we chose him. Was it a divorce?!"

As for His words: ﴿So come, I will provide for you﴾, i.e., the provision (mut'ah) of divorce, and we have explained this in Surah al-Baqarah.

As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿And release you with a beautiful release﴾: the beautiful release (al-sarah al-jamil) is a graceful separation, without reproach and without harm.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you desire God and His Messenger and the Last Abode, then indeed God has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward﴾. The "good-doers" (al-muhsinat) are those who chose God, His Messenger and the Last Abode, and all the wives of the Prophet have chosen that, so all of them are good-doers. It is also permissible for "min" (some of) to be mentioned without being partitive (tab'id), so that this does not indicate that among them there are some who are not good-doers.

His saying: ﴿a great reward﴾. It is mentioned in the tafsir that God, exalted is He, gave them the choice between this world and the Hereafter, and between Paradise and Hellfire, so they chose the Hereafter over this world, and Paradise over Hellfire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 30:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear indecency﴾. If it is said: Does this address indicate that some of them have committed, or will commit, an indecency? We say: No, just as God Almighty said to the Prophet: ﴿If you were to associate partners with God, your deeds would surely be nullified﴾, and this does not indicate that he has committed or will commit polytheism.

Another answer: It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Al-fahisha (indecency) here means nushuz (disobedience/ill conduct toward the husband) and bad character."

As for His words: ﴿Her punishment will be doubled, twofold﴾. It was recited as "yudda'af" (from tadh'if, doubling), and it was recited as "nudda'af" with the nun. The statement ﴿nudda'af﴾ with the nun is clear in meaning, as it attributes the action to Himself, while "yud'af" and "yudaa'af" are in the passive, as a report.

His words: ﴿twofold of the punishment﴾, meaning double the punishment of others. If it is said: Why does she deserve double the punishment of others? We say: Because of the nobility of her station through companionship with the Prophet (ﷺ). This is like how a free woman receives double the hadd punishment of a slave woman because of the nobility of her station. Abu Bakr al-Farisi, in Ahkam al-Qur'an, used this verse as evidence that they are the most noble women of the world.

His words: ﴿And that is easy for God﴾, meaning: effortless. Some scholars mentioned that His words ﴿her punishment will be doubled﴾ imply three punishments, since double of one is two times, but the more correct view is the first.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 31:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever of you devoutly obeys (yaqnut) Allah and His Messenger﴾. Qunut is persistence in obedience, and from it comes qunut in prayer, which is persistence in supplication.

And His saying: ﴿and does righteous deeds, We will give her reward twice﴾, meaning, twice the reward of others, and this is in the manner of matching reward against punishment.

And His saying: ﴿and We have prepared for her a generous provision﴾, meaning, Paradise.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 32:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among the women﴾. If it is said: why did He not say "like one of the women"? The answer: He said "like anyone among the women" so that it would be more general in encompassing all of them.

And His saying: ﴿if you fear Allah﴾. Taqwa (God-consciousness, piety) is refraining from acts of disobedience and guarding oneself against what Allah has forbidden.

And His saying: ﴿so do not be soft in speech﴾. That is: do not be gentle in speech, and do not be tender in it. It is said: submissiveness in speech is that you speak in a manner that arouses the desire of the one with doubt in his heart.

And His saying: ﴿lest he in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾. Qatadah said: that is hypocrisy. Ikrimah said: the desire for fornication.

And His saying: ﴿and speak a known word﴾. That is: speech that religion and Islam require, with clarity and explanation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 33:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And stay in your houses﴾. It was also read with a kasra on the qaf (waqirna, from waqara), so his saying with the kasra means tranquillity, calm, and abstaining from going out. The reading with a fatha (waqarna) allows this meaning, and it also allows the meaning of a command to dignity and gravity (al-waqar).

It is reported from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "No woman has worshipped Allah with the like of the piety of Allah and of sitting in her house."

In some reports it is said that Sawda was asked: "Will you not go out as your sisters have gone out?" She said: "I have performed the Hajj and the 'umrah, and Allah Exalted has commanded me to remain in my house, so I do not wish to disobey Allah Exalted." So she did not leave her house until she was carried out on her funeral bier.

His saying: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance (tabarruj al-jahiliyyah al-ula)﴾. Al-Mubarrad said: tabarruj is that a woman displays of herself what she has been commanded to conceal. It is reported from Ibn Abi Najih that he said: it is at-tabakhtur (strutting, swaggering). It is reported from Qatadah that he said: walking with coquetry and affectation. It is reported from Mujahid that he said: walking before men.

As for al-Jahiliyyah al-Ula (the first age of ignorance), it is said: it is the era of Namrud, when a woman would go out wearing a shirt of pearls which she had sewn up at the sides. It is reported from some of them: it is the period between Nuh and Idris. It is reported from al-Sha'bi: it is the period between Isa and Muhammad, upon them be blessings and peace. It is also said: the first appearance of immorality among the children of Adam was that there were two clans of the children of Adam, one of which inhabited the mountain and the other the plain. The men of the mountain were handsome, and there was ugliness among the women; the women of the plain were beautiful, and there was ugliness among the men. Iblis devised a stratagem until they took a festival, and he gathered them together, and some of them committed immorality with others. Some of them mentioned that in the first age of ignorance [a woman would be] between two men, her lower half belonging to one of them and her upper half to the other, so that the woman was joined to her husband and her lover. Some of them said poetry about this:

(Do you desire the exchange, Abu Jubayr, and are you content with the young women and the old woman?)

As for the other ignorance (al-jahiliyyah al-ukhra), it refers to a people who do like their deeds, and that will be at the end of time. Some of them said: it is permissible to mention "the first" even if there is no other, do you not see that Allah Exalted said: ﴿And that He destroyed the first 'Ad﴾, and there was no other 'Ad.

His saying: ﴿And establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾: its meaning is apparent.

His saying: ﴿Allah only wants to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾. In the verse there are several opinions. Sa'id ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn Abbas that it was revealed concerning the wives of the Prophet, and 'Ikrimah and a group said it.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Umm Salamah, and a large group of the Successors, including Mujahid, Qatadah and others, held that the verse concerns the People of the House of the Prophet, namely 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn.

Umm Salamah narrated that the Prophet was in her house, and with him were 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and Allah revealed this verse, so he covered them with a cloak and said: "O Allah, these are the people of my house." Umm Salamah said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, and am I of the people of your house?" He said: "You are on the good." Abu 'Isa mentioned it in his Jami'.

He also narrated through the route of Anas that the Prophet used to pass by the house of Fatimah for six months after the revelation of this verse, saying: "Allah only wants to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification."

Those who held this view argued that Allah Exalted said: ﴿Allah only wants to remove from you the uncleanness﴾ and did not say "from you" (feminine plural, "ankunna"). Had the intended meaning been the wives of the Prophet, He would have said "ankunna." Do you not see that at the beginning and at the end, since the address was with the wives of the Prophet, He addressed them with feminine address?

The third opinion: the verse is general to all of them, and this is the best of the sayings, for his family have entered into the verse and his wives have entered into the verse. Those who argued that his wives have entered into the verse said: He said: ﴿Allah only wants to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the household﴾, and the people of the Messenger's household are his wives; (and because the mention of his wives preceded it). The best is what we have explained, namely generalization.

It is reported that Zayd ibn Arqam was asked: "Who are the family (al) of the Prophet?" He said: "They are those upon whom charity has been made unlawful." As for ar-rijs, its meaning is: that which calls to disobedience. Some of them said: the work of Satan. Ar-rijs in the language is every thing that is filthy and loathsome.

His saying: ﴿and purify you with complete purification﴾, that is, from sins through the piety of Allah Exalted. Some of the (adherents of) spiritual intuitions (ashab al-khawatir) held that the meaning of His saying ﴿Allah wants to remove from you the uncleanness﴾ is the caprices and innovations, ﴿and purify you with complete purification﴾ by the Sunnah. Some of them said: "remove from you the uncleanness" means envy and jealousy, "and purify you with complete purification" by success and guidance. Some of them said: "remove from you the uncleanness" means stinginess and greed, "and purify you with complete purification" by contentment and altruism. The interpretation is what we have explained before.

Almighty God's words: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and the wisdom﴾, meaning: the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, God is Subtle, Acquainted﴾, meaning: merciful to them, aware of their deeds.

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and the Muslim women﴾. The occasion of revelation of the verse is what is related that Umm Salama said: "O Messenger of Allah, why is it that men are mentioned in the Qur'an but women are not mentioned? We fear that there is no good in them."

In another narration, from Asma bint Umays: she came from Abyssinia and entered upon the wives of the Prophet and said to them: "Has Allah the Exalted mentioned women with good in the Qur'an?" They said: "No." She said: "Then this is ﴿and the patient men and the patient women, and the humble men and the humble women, and the charitable men and the charitable women, and the fasting men and the fasting women﴾ the failure and loss. I fear that Allah has no need of them." Then she came to the Prophet and mentioned that to him.

In a third narration: "The one who said that was Umm Umara al-Ansariyya, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, and mentioned women with good as He mentioned men."

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and the Muslim women, and the believing men and the believing women﴾. We have already explained the meaning of Islam and the meaning of faith (iman). Some of the People of the Sunna (Ahl al-Sunna, the adherents of the Prophetic tradition) distinguished between faith and Islam, and some did not. The matter has much discussion.

And His saying: ﴿and the obedient men and the obedient women﴾: the obedient men and the obedient women.

And His saying: ﴿and the truthful men and the truthful women﴾: that is, the men truthful in their faith and the women truthful in their faith. It is said that what is meant by truthfulness is truthfulness of speech in all matters.

And His saying: ﴿and the patient men and the patient women﴾: that is, the men patient in obedience and patient against disobedience, and likewise the meaning of the patient women.

Qatada said: patience against disobedience is better than patience in obedience, and most scholars hold this view.

And His saying: ﴿and the humble men and the humble women﴾: that is, the men who are modest and the women who are modest. It is said that what is meant by humility (khushu') is humility in prayer.

From Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "Humility in prayer is that one does not know who is on his right or who is on his left." ﴿and the fasting women and the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard, and the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember, Allah has prepared﴾ Someone else said: "Of humility is that one does not turn his head."

And His saying: ﴿and the charitable men and the charitable women﴾: that is, the men who give charity to the poor and the women who give charity to them.

And His saying: ﴿and the fasting men and the fasting women﴾ is known. It has been related from some of them: whoever fasts three days in every month is one of the fasting men and women, and whoever gives a dirham in charity every week is one of the charitable, and whoever does not turn his head in his prayer is one of the humble. This was recorded by al-Naqqash in his tafsir.

And His saying: ﴿and the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard﴾: that is, from committing indecencies.

Al-Naqqash related that whoever does not commit adultery is one of those who guard their private parts.

And His saying: ﴿and the women who guard﴾: that is, those who guard them (their private parts).

And His saying: ﴿and the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember﴾: that is, and the women who remember Him. The poet said:

(So her two shins are stained with blood, as if over them / there ran a golden hue, and she took on its colour.)

He means: a golden hue ran over them, and she took on its colour.

As for much remembrance of Allah, it was related from Mujahid that he said: a servant does not become one of those who remember Allah much until he remembers Him standing, sitting, and lying on his side.

Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim related, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet said: "Whoever says: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest, and there is no power nor strength except through Allah, he is recorded among those who remember Allah much, and his sins fall away from him as leaves fall from a tree, and Allah looks at him, and whoever is looked at by Him, (He) will not punish him."

In some of the Musnads, through the narration of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, the Prophet said: "Whichever man wakes his wife at night, and they both stand and perform ablution and pray two rak'as, they are both recorded among those who remember Allah much, and the women who remember."

And His saying: ﴿Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward﴾: that is, forgiveness of sins, and a great reward, which is Paradise.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 36:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman﴾, the verse was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh and her brother Abdullah ibn Jahsh. They were both children of the paternal aunt of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was Umaymah bint Abd al-Muttalib. On their father's side, they were from the Banu Asad, from the descendants of Ghanm ibn Dudan.

It was narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) proposed marriage to Zaynab on behalf of Zayd ibn Harithah, his freedman. She disliked that and said: "I am the daughter of your paternal aunt; will you marry me to your freedman?" Her brother likewise disliked it, so Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse: ﴿It is not for a believing man﴾, meaning Abdullah ibn Jahsh, ﴿or a believing woman﴾, meaning Zaynab.

As for His words: ﴿When Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter﴾, meaning: when Allah and His Messenger intend a matter, and that matter is the marriage of Zayd to Zaynab.

As for His words: ﴿they have no choice in their affair﴾, meaning: they have no option of choosing. The meaning is: that they should desire other than what Allah desired, or refrain from what Allah and His Messenger have commanded them.

As for His words: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error﴾, meaning: he has erred with an evident error.

When they heard that, they submitted to the matter, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married her to Zayd ibn Harithah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 37:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when you said to the one on whom Allah had bestowed favour﴾, i.e., Allah had bestowed favour upon him with Islam.

And His saying: ﴿and you had bestowed favour upon him﴾, i.e., with manumission. He was Zayd ibn Harithah, who had been taken captive in the Jahiliyyah, and the Messenger of Allah bought him, freed him, and adopted him, in accordance with the custom of the Arabs.

And His saying: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾, i.e., your woman. As for the occasion of the revelation of this verse: "When the Prophet had married Zaynab to Zayd, and some time passed, the Messenger of Allah entered upon her one day and saw her standing. She was fair and beautiful, of good character, and she was wearing a shift and a head-covering. When he saw her, she fell into his heart and her beauty pleased him, and he said: 'Glory be to the One who turns the hearts.' Zaynab heard that, and the Messenger of Allah went out with what was in his heart, by the will of Allah. When Zayd entered upon her, she told him about that." And in some of the exegeses: "Zayd came complaining about Zaynab, for she was a woman with a sharp tongue, so the Messenger of Allah went to admonish her, and the matter was as we have mentioned. Then Zayd came to the Messenger of Allah and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I complain to you about the bad character of Zaynab, and that she has arrogance, and I want to divorce her.' The Messenger of Allah said to him: 'Keep your wife to yourself, i.e., your woman, and fear Allah regarding her matter.'"

﴿...what Allah is to bring to light, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had accomplished his need from her﴾

And His saying: ﴿and you concealed within yourself what Allah is to bring to light﴾. Qatadah said: it is his love for her. Al-Hasan said: the Prophet wished for her divorce but did not show it. 'Ali ibn al-Husayn mentioned that the meaning of the verse is that Allah had informed him that Zayd would divorce her and that he would then marry her, so what he concealed was this. This view is the preferred one and more fitting to the infallibility of the Prophets. Some said: what he concealed within himself was that if Zayd divorced her, he would marry her. This is also a good view.

And His saying: ﴿and you feared the people﴾, i.e., you felt shy before the people. It is said: you feared the people's speech and their blame, and that they would say he had married his son's wife.

And His saying: ﴿while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾. If it is said: this indicates that he did not fear Allah in what had preceded from him in this story. The answer is in two ways. The first: the meaning of His saying ﴿while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ is a general statement concerning all matters, and Allah the Exalted has commanded all His servants to fear Him in all circumstances.

The second answer: you concealed something and did not show it; so if you feared Allah in showing it, then fear Him in concealing it. The true meaning is: there is no fear except of Allah, in what you show and in what you conceal, so do not be mindful of the people.

If it is said: since he wished to divorce her, how did he say "Keep your wife to yourself"? The answer: that wish was a wish of nature and inclination of the soul, and human beings are not free of it.

As for His saying: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah﴾, it is a command to what is right, and there is no sin upon him for what falls into his heart without his choice. Moreover, we have mentioned other views besides this. It has been established by the narration of Masruq from ʿAʾishah that she said: "If the Prophet had concealed any part of the revelation, he would have concealed this verse." And it has been related that no verse was harder upon him than this one.

And His saying: ﴿So when Zayd had accomplished his need from her, We gave her to you in marriage﴾. In the exegesis: when Zayd was informed of the matter, he divorced her. Some have mentioned that the Prophet left her until her ʿiddah ended, then married her.

Most exegeses do not mention an ʿiddah, nor a marriage by a guardian; what is transmitted is that Zayd divorced her and that Allah married her to him, and this is evident.

His saying: ﴿So when Zayd had accomplished his need from her, We gave her to you in marriage﴾. And His saying: ﴿wataran (need)﴾, i.e., need, and it is reaching the limit of what is in the soul. The poet said:

(O rider, hasten with the swift camel... the needs have been fulfilled from Tihamah)

And Jarir said:

(The companion departed at dawn at al-Jinab, and your soul has not fulfilled its needs)

It is established in the two Sahihs that Zaynab used to boast over the rest of the wives of the Prophet and say: "Your guardians married you off, but Allah married me from above the seven heavens."

It has been narrated that when the Prophet wished to marry her, he sent Zayd to propose to her. Zayd entered upon her and proposed on behalf of the Messenger of Allah. She said: "Not until I consult my Lord," and she stood up to her place of prayer, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿So when Zayd had accomplished his need from her, We gave her to you in marriage﴾. This is a well-known report. The people of tafsir said: "When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah came and entered upon her without permission, and he held a wedding feast for her with bread and meat." It has been established by the narration of Anas that the Prophet held no feast for any of his wives as he held for Zaynab bint Jahsh; he satisfied the people with bread and meat.

Among the virtues of Zaynab: the Prophet said to his wives at the time of his death: "The swiftest of you to join me will be the longest of you in hand," so Zaynab was the first of the wives of the Prophet to die after him. She was a woman who worked with her hands and gave much charity from the earnings of her hand, so they understood that the meaning of "long hand" was abundance of charity.

She was also the first to have a bier (na'sh) made for her. It is narrated that when she died in the time of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, and she was a woman of noble disposition, ʿUmar disliked that she should be carried out as men are carried out; so Asma' bint ʿUmays sent the bier, and ʿUmar ordered it to be made, and she was carried out on the bier. ʿUmar said: "This is indeed the litter of the traveling woman." Thereafter the practice continued in this way until our day. They said: Asma' had seen this in Abyssinia.

His saying: ﴿so that there may be no discomfort for the believers﴾, i.e., no sin.

His saying: ﴿concerning the wives of their adopted sons﴾, i.e., concerning the women whom they adopt. The Arabs considered that forbidden, so Allah abrogated adoption and made lawful the wives of the adopted sons (al-mutabannin).

His saying: ﴿when they have accomplished their need from them﴾ has been discussed.

His saying: ﴿And the command of Allah is ever accomplished﴾, i.e., the decree of Allah is executed and cannot be turned back.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is no blame upon the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him﴾, meaning: in what Allah has made lawful for him.

And His saying: ﴿[It is] the way of Allah with those who passed on before﴾, meaning: [it is] like the way of Allah with those who passed on before. When the preposition was removed, the noun took the accusative (fa-lamma naza'a al-khafid intasaba). It was also said that it is in the accusative as an incitement (al-ighra'), as if he had said: "Adhere to the way of Allah."

As for His saying: ﴿with those who passed on before﴾, meaning: David and Solomon, we have already explained the number of wives that David and Solomon had. Some [scholars] mentioned that the purpose of the verse is to liken the state of the Prophet to the state of David, for David desired a woman and Allah brought them together in a lawful manner; likewise, the Messenger desired a woman and Allah brought them together in a lawful manner.

His saying: ﴿And the command of Allah is a decree decreed﴾, meaning: a judgment that has been judged.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 39:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him, and fear no one except Allah﴾. That is: a fear that comes between them and disobedience to Him, and this is the true meaning of khashya (fear, awe).

And His saying: ﴿and fear no one except Allah﴾, that is, other than Allah. Its meaning is that they do not hold anyone in regard concerning what He has made lawful for them. In some (narrations) (al-athar) it is said: whoever is not shy before Allah regarding what He has made lawful for him, his burden (mu'na) will be light.

And His saying: ﴿and Allah suffices as a reckoner (hasib)﴾, that is, a guardian (hafiz). It is also said: one who calls to account (muhasib). The Arabs say: "ahsabanı" (al-shay'), meaning it sufficed me.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 40:

The words of God, Exalted: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾. Most of the exegetes hold that what is meant is Zayd ibn Harithah, and its meaning is that he is not the father of Zayd ibn Harithah. If it is said: Did he not have male and female children, and were not al-Hasan and al-Husayn his sons?

It is established from the Prophet that he said to al-Hasan ibn Ali: "Verily this son of mine is a master (sayyid); through him God will reconcile two great factions of the Muslims."

In this there is an allusion to the reconciliation (sulh) that took place between the people of Iraq and the people of Syria when al-Hasan pledged allegiance to Mu'awiyah and handed over the affair to him, and the story is well known. The answer to this is in two respects. The first: the meaning of His words ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾ is: not the father of a man whom he begot, and Zayd ibn Harithah was not his son; so he was not his father. He did have male children, who were born to him, namely: al-Qasim, al-Tayyib, al-Tahir, and Ibrahim, may God be pleased with them all; and some have substituted al-Mutahhir for al-Tahir.

The second answer: He said ﴿of your men﴾, and these were children, whereas "rijal" (men) is a term that applies to adults. 'Ata' related from Ibn 'Abbas that when God, Exalted, decreed that there would be no prophet after him, He did not grant him a male child who would reach manhood; for had He granted him a male child who reached manhood, He would have made him a prophet.

Some scholars have said: This is not objectionable, and it is possible that he had a son who reached manhood and was not a prophet. What we have mentioned is related from Ibn 'Abbas, and God knows best.

As for His words ﴿but the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets﴾: it has been recited "khatam" with a fatha on the ta'. As for ﴿khatam al-nabiyyin﴾ with a fatha, it means: the last of the prophets; and with a kasra (khatim), it means: the one through whom the prophets were sealed.

His words ﴿and God is ever Knowing of all things﴾ mean: Knowing. It has been established by the narration of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of me and the prophets before me is like a man who built a house and completed it and beautified it, except for the place of one brick in it. So everyone who enters the house says: How beautiful and complete it is, were it not for the place of that brick. So I am the brick, and there is no prophet after me."

And among the strange reports: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not come until there are sent forth nearly thirty deceivers and liars, each of whom claims that he is a prophet, and there is no prophet after me."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 41:

The words of God Most High: ﴿O you who have believed, remember God with much remembrance﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions. The first is that the intended "much remembrance" is the five daily prayers (salawat). The second is that the intended "much remembrance" is glorification (tasbih), praising (tahmid), declaring God's oneness (tahlil), magnifying (takbir), and the like, and these are the remembrances that no Muslim is prevented from reciting, whether in a state of major ritual impurity (janabah), minor ritual impurity (hadath), or any other condition. Some of them said: the much remembrance takes place in the heart, and it is the remembrance by which one perpetuates obedience to God and by which one is restrained from disobeying Him.

And His saying: ﴿And glorify Him morning and evening﴾ means: pray to God in the morning and the evening. Al-asil (the late afternoon, evening) is what lies between the ʿasr (afternoon) prayer and the maghrib (sunset) prayer. It is also said that the prayers of al-asil are the ẓuhr (noon), ʿasr (afternoon), maghrib (sunset) and ʿishā' (night) prayers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 43:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels [do likewise]﴾. The scholars have differed concerning the meaning of "ṣalawāt" (blessings) when attributed to Allah, exalted is He. Abu al-'Aliyah said: it is praise from Allah upon His servants. Some of them (narrated) from him: it is the spreading of a good remembrance of them. The most well-known of the statements is that the blessing from Allah, exalted is He, means mercy and forgiveness, while the blessing of the angels means seeking forgiveness for the believers. Al-Hasan al-Basri mentioned that the Children of Israel said to Musa, peace be upon him: "Does your Lord send blessings?" So Musa mentioned that to Allah, exalted is He, and Allah, exalted is He, said: "Indeed I send blessings, and My blessings are that My mercy has preceded My wrath."

In some exegeses: when Allah, exalted is He, revealed His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾, the Companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is for you! So what is for us?" Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels [do likewise]﴾.

And His saying: ﴿that He may bring you out from the darknesses into the light﴾, meaning: from the darkness of misguidance into the light of guidance, and from the darkness of disbelief into the light of faith. It was also said: from the darkness of the Fire into the light of Paradise.

And His saying: ﴿And He is ever Merciful to the believers﴾, meaning: by what He has decreed for them of happiness.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 44:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him will be, "Peace."﴾ There are several opinions on this. The first: the meaning of "meet Him" is that they meet Allah, may He be exalted, and the peace from Allah to them is the affirmation of everlasting safety and security from calamities. It was also said: Allah Himself greets them with peace.

The second opinion: the meaning of His saying "meet Him" is the Angel of Death, peace be upon him, and the pronoun refers to something not mentioned, which occurs in many places in the Qur'an. Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib said: "There is no believer except that the Angel of Death greets him with peace when he intends to seize his soul." The third opinion: what is meant is the greeting of the angels, and its meaning is that when they are raised, the angels of Allah greet them with peace and give them the good news of Paradise.

His saying: ﴿And He has prepared for them a generous reward.﴾ That is, Paradise. Know that reports have come urging the remembrance of Allah, may He be exalted, among them what is firmly established from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "Allah, may He be exalted, says: I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me."

It is also firmly established from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "Allah, may He be exalted, says: If My servant remembers Me in his self, I remember him in My Self; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than theirs..." the report.
