In some of the Musnads, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever is too weak to stay up in the night to worship, and too cowardly to strive against the enemy, and too stingy to spend his wealth, then let him devote himself to the remembrance of Allah, may He be exalted."

O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness (شَاهدا), meaning: a witness over the conveying of the messengers of their Lord's message.

And His words, ﴿and a bearer of good news﴾, meaning: of Paradise; and His words, ﴿and a warner﴾, meaning: from the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 46:

And His saying: ﴿And as one who calls to Allah⌋ means: to Islam. It is also said: to the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

And His saying: ﴿by His permission﴾ means: by His command. And His saying: ﴿and as a shining lamp﴾ means: possessing a illuminating lamp, and the illuminating lamp is the Qur'an. It is also said that "a shining lamp" is the Messenger (ﷺ); he was called a lamp because he is guided by him, just as a lamp is used for light, as the poet said:

(Indeed the Messenger is a light by which one is illuminated, / a sharp sword drawn from the swords of Allah.)

And His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty.﴾ It is related that when Allah the Exalted revealed His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have given you, [O Muhammad], a clear conquest, that Allah may forgive you your previous and subsequent sins﴾, the Companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is for you; what is for us?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 48:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾. The disbelievers: Abu Sufyan, and Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, who later embraced Islam, and Abu al-A'war al-Sulami. The hypocrites: Abdullah ibn Ubayy, Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq, and Ibn (Sifnah), and their like.

And His saying: ﴿And leave off their harm﴾. Mujahid said: Be patient over their harm. It is said that this verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword (naskh, abrogation).

And His saying: ﴿And put your trust in Allah﴾, i.e., have confidence in Allah.

And His saying: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a Disposer of affairs﴾, i.e., as a Guardian.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 49:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them﴾ In the verse there is evidence that divorce is not permissible before marriage, because He linked divorce to marriage, which indicates that divorce does not precede it. This meaning has been related from Ibn 'Abbas.

It has also been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no divorce before marriage." This strengthens what we have mentioned regarding the derivation from the verse.

His saying: ﴿before you have touched them, then you have no waiting period for them that you should count﴾ In the verse there is evidence that if he divorces before consummation (dukhul), no waiting period ('iddah) is obligatory. As for when he has been alone with the woman and then divorces her, is the 'iddah obligatory? There is a well-known difference of opinion on this question, as is known.

His saying: ﴿that you should count﴾ means: that you should complete its term.

His saying: ﴿then provide for them﴾ We have already explained provision (mut'ah) in Surat al-Baqarah. It has been said by some that this verse is abrogated (mansukh) by His saying: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, while you have already appointed for them an obligation, then half of what you have appointed﴾. For this reason, half of the stipulated dowry is obligatory when divorce occurs before consummation, and provision is not obligatory; rather, provision is obligatory for the divorced woman for whom half of the stipulated dowry is not obligatory.

His saying: ﴿and release them with a fair release﴾. The fair release (tasrih jamil) is divorce together with the discharge of the rights.

**Tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) of al-Sam'ani on surah 33, verse 50:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have given their bridal payments﴾. That is: their dowries (mahr).

His saying: ﴿and what your right hand possesses of what Allah has bestowed upon you﴾. That is: what Allah has granted you as booty. It is said: what Allah returned to you from the disbelievers. Among what Allah bestowed upon him were Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Juwayriyya bint Abi Dirar al-Mustaliqiyya. Mariya was also among what his right hand possessed, and he had a son by her, Ibrahim.

His saying: ﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncle﴾. That is: the children of Abd al-Muttalib.

﴿...the daughters of your paternal uncle, the daughters of your paternal aunts, the daughters of your maternal uncle, and the daughters of your maternal aunts, who emigrated with you, and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet wishes to marry her, exclusively for you, not for the believers...﴾

His saying: ﴿the daughters of your paternal aunts﴾. That is: from the children of the daughters of Abd al-Muttalib.

His saying: ﴿the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts﴾. That is: from the children of Abd Manaf ibn Zuhra ibn Kilab.

His saying: ﴿who emigrated with you﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions. The first: they embraced Islam with you. This implies that a non-Muslim woman is not lawful to him, even if she is a Jewess or a Christian, whereas she is lawful for his community. The second opinion: they emigrated with you to Medina. The verse then implies that a woman who did not emigrate is not lawful to him. Regarding its meaning there are two opinions: the first is that a woman who did not emigrate is not lawful to him, whether a stranger or a relative. The second is that a woman who did not emigrate is not lawful to him among the relatives and those he mentioned, but among strangers she is lawful.

Abu Salih reported from Umm Hani that when the Messenger of Allah conquered Mecca, he proposed to me, and Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, so I was not lawful to him, because I was not among the emigrants, and I was among the Tulaqa'. Umm Hani was the sister of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.

His saying: ﴿and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾. It was also read: "in wahabat" with a fatha (in waahabat), since with a kasra it is general, and with a fatha it refers to a specific woman.

From Ibn Abbas, he said: None of the women whom the Prophet kept (in marriage) was one who had given herself to him.

From another source: Maymuna bint al-Harith was among those who gave themselves, and among those who gave themselves was Umm Sharik, who was a righteous woman. It is reported that she became thirsty during a journey, so Allah the Exalted sent down to her a bucket from heaven, and she hung an empty waterskin, and it was filled with ghee. It is said: "Among the signs of Allah is the waterskin of Umm Sharik." It was said that the Messenger of Allah had known her to be beautiful, so he asked about her on the day of the conquest of Mecca. This reached her, so she came and gave herself to the Prophet, but he did not see her as he had known her, so he left her.

From Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her: Khawla bint Hakim was among those who gave themselves to the Prophet.

From al-Sha'bi: the one who gave herself to the Prophet was Zaynab bint Khuzayma al-Ansariyya, Umm al-Masakin.

His saying: ﴿if the Prophet wishes to marry her﴾. That is: seeks to marry her.

His saying: ﴿exclusively for you, not for the believers﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions. The first: the meaning of "exclusively" is that she is lawful to you without a dowry, and not lawful to anyone else without a dowry. This is the view of Ikrima and a group. The second opinion: the meaning of his saying ﴿exclusively for you﴾ is that the permissibility of marriage by the wording of gift is exclusive to you. This is attributed to al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him.

His saying: ﴿We have certainly known what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives﴾. That is: what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives of the rulings. The rulings are that marriage is not permissible except with witnesses, a guardian, a dowry, and the completion of the waiting period (iddah), and similar matters.

His saying: ﴿and what their right hands possess﴾. That is: and what We have made obligatory of the rulings concerning what their right hands possess.

His saying: "(﴿upon them and﴾ their right hands)" refers to the believers.

His saying: ﴿so that there will be no difficulty for you﴾. That is: constraint. The meaning is: We have made the matter easy for you, so that there will be no difficulty upon you.

His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾. It has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 51:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You may put off whom you wish of them﴾ has three opinions. The first: "You divorce whom you wish of them, and take to you whom you wish," meaning: you keep whom you wish of them. This is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. The second opinion: "You put off whom you wish of them" means: you do not marry them. And His saying, ﴿and take to you whom you wish﴾, means: whom you wish to marry. The third opinion: "You put off whom you wish of them" means: you delay them, so they are excluded from the turn (qasm, the rotation of nights among the wives).

And His saying, ﴿and take to you whom you wish﴾, means: you bring them into the turn. This is the most well-known of the opinions. It is as if God, exalted is He, permitted him to allot turns to whom he wished and to leave whom he wished of them. Then scholars differed as to whether he excluded any of them from the turn. One of the two opinions is that he excluded none of them from the turn. The second opinion, related by Abu Razin, is that he excluded five and allotted turns to four. The five whom he excluded were: Sawda, Umm Habiba, Safiyya, Juwayriya and Maymuna. Those to whom he allotted turns were: ʿA'isha, Hafsa, Umm Salama and Zaynab. The more apparent of the opinions is the first.

It has been narrated that "during his final illness he would go round his wives until they consented that he be nursed in the house of ʿA'isha."

His saying, ﴿and whomever you seek out of those you have set aside﴾, means: whomever you saw among them and had postponed, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, means: there is no sin upon you.

His saying, ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted and they not grieve, and that they be pleased with what you give them, all of them﴾, its meaning: when they know that this is from what God, exalted is He, has revealed, it is more pleasing to their souls, less grievous to them, and closer to their contentment. It is also said: when they know that you have the right to take to yourself whom you wish, then whomever you set aside is closer to what we have mentioned. In some tafsirs: "The Prophet intended to divorce a group of his wives, so they said to him: leave us in our state, and allot turns as you wish."

His saying, ﴿And God knows what is in your hearts, and God is ever Knowing, Forbearing﴾, means: Knowing of the affairs of His creation, Forbearing toward the actions of His creatures.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 52:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this]﴾. It has already been explained that when God, may He be exalted, commanded His Messenger to give his wives the choice, and they chose God, His Messenger and the Last Abode, He thanked them for their choice and forbade him any women other than them, and prohibited him from exchanging them. Then the scholars differed over whether women were made lawful to him after that or not. It is related from ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, that she said: "The Messenger of God did not pass away until women had been made lawful to him."

The second view: the prohibition remained until the Prophet passed away.

As for His saying: ﴿And even if their beauty impressed you﴾, its meaning is clear. There is another view regarding this verse, which is what is related from Mujahid, that he said: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this], nor to exchange them for other wives﴾ means: it is not permitted for you to choose non-Muslim women over Muslim women, and its meaning is that it is not permissible for him to marry a Jewish woman or a Christian woman. In some of the exegetical works it is mentioned that the woman who impressed him was Asmaʾ bint ʿUmays al-Khathʿamiyyah, who had been married to Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib. When he was martyred, the Prophet wished to propose to her, but he forbade him from doing so.

As for His saying: ﴿except what your right hand possesses﴾, it means: apart from what your right hand possesses. And His saying: ﴿And God is over all things Watcher﴾ means: Guardian (ḥafīẓ).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 53:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet﴾. The occasion of revelation of the verse: it is related that the Companions used to enter the houses of the Prophet without permission, waiting for the food to be ready. When they had finished eating, they sat talking and prolonged their sitting. The Prophet (ﷺ) would be troubled by them and feel shy before them. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse and taught them this etiquette between themselves and the Prophet (ﷺ).

It is also established through the narration of Anas that "the Prophet (ﷺ) held a wedding feast (walima) for Zaynab bint Jahsh and invited his Companions. When they had finished and went out, two men remained sitting and talking. The Prophet (ﷺ) wished that they would leave so that he could be alone with his wife, but they did not leave." In another narration: he went out several times so that they would follow him, but they still did not leave. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. It is also well known that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) did not veil themselves from men, according to the custom of the Arabs. Umar used to say: "O Messenger of Allah, veil your wives, for both the righteous and the wicked enter upon you." The women used to go out at night to the open areas (al-manasi') for their needs. Sawda went out one night, and she was a tall woman. Umar said: "We have recognised you, O Sawda," raising his voice, eager that the veil be revealed. So Allah the Exalted revealed the verse of the hijab. It is also well known that "the Prophet (ﷺ) was eating hays (a dish of dates, butter and cheese) with Aisha, when Umar passed by and he called him, and he began to eat with them. His finger touched Aisha's finger, and Umar said: 'Hass (an exclamation of discomfort); if only you were obeyed regarding yourselves, no eye would see you.' Then the verse of the hijab was revealed."

﴿Without lingering for conversation. Indeed, that would be troublesome to the Prophet, and he would be shy of you, but Allah is not shy of the truth. And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a screen. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾

And His words: ﴿not waiting for its preparation﴾, meaning: its readiness and ripeness. The poet said:

(The fates have writhed for him on a day... and every bearer of a child has its term)

And His words: ﴿but when you are invited, enter﴾.

And His words: ﴿and when you have eaten, disperse﴾. Al-Hasan al-Basri and others said: the verse was revealed concerning the burdensome guests. It is related from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i: whoever knows that he is burdensome is not burdensome.

And His words: ﴿nor lingering for conversation﴾, meaning: they should not sit in the house of the Prophet after finishing the meal, talking and enjoying conversation.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, that would be troublesome to the Prophet, and he would be shy of you﴾, meaning: he would be shy of asking you to leave.

And His words: ﴿but Allah is not shy of the truth﴾, meaning: He does not abandon the explanation of the truth [and mention it] out of shyness.

And His words: ﴿And when you ask them for something﴾, meaning: a need.

And His words: ﴿ask them from behind a screen﴾, meaning: from behind a curtain. In the exegesis it is stated that after the verse of the hijab, it was not permissible for anyone to look at any of the wives of the Prophet, whether they were veiled or not, because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿from behind a screen﴾. It is related that when Aisha circumambulated (the Ka'ba), they would screen off the area behind her.

And His words: ﴿That is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾, meaning: purer from doubt.

And His words: ﴿And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾. The people of exegesis said: when the verse of the hijab was revealed and men were prevented from entering the houses of the Prophet, a man from among the Companions said: "What is the matter with us, being prevented from entering upon our paternal cousins? By Allah, if anything happens to him, I will certainly marry Aisha." Most scholars hold that the one who said this was Talha ibn Ubayd Allah, who was of the kin of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.

That statement was a lapse on his part; so Allah the Exalted revealed [this His word]: ﴿And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾.

And His words: ﴿nor that you should marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of Allah an enormity﴾, meaning: a grave sin.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 54:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Whether you disclose a thing or conceal it﴾. What was disclosed and made apparent was the saying of that speaker: "What is wrong with us that we are prevented from entering upon the daughters of our paternal uncles?"

As for His words: ﴿or conceal it﴾, what was concealed is his inner intention to marry ʿĀʾisha after the Prophet. It is narrated that he did not say this, but he harboured it inwardly.

As for His words: ﴿indeed Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing﴾, meaning: Knowing. In the tafsir of al-Naqqash: the Prophet (ﷺ) delivered a sermon after the revelation of this verse and said: "O people, indeed Allah has preferred me over all men, and He has preferred my wives over all women, and indeed Allah has forbidden them to you and made them like your mothers. So do not transgress His limits, lest He punish you with a painful torment. Behold, the best of my wives is ʿĀʾisha bint Abi Bakr, except for Khadija bint Khuwaylid. And indeed Fatima is the mistress of the women of the worlds, except for Mary bint ʿImran. And al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, are the masters of the youths of the people of Paradise. And indeed Abu Bakr and ʿUmar are the masters of the elders of the people of Paradise, except for the Prophets and the Messengers."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 55:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers﴾ – the verse. It is related that when the first verse was revealed, the fathers and the sons stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is our status? Shall we enter upon them or not?" So Allah, Exalted is He, revealed His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon them﴾, meaning: there is no sin upon them, ﴿concerning their fathers, nor their sons, nor their brothers, nor the sons of their brothers, nor the sons of their sisters﴾. If it is said: He did not mention the paternal uncles, and by consensus it is permissible for the paternal uncles to enter upon them. Since He said ﴿concerning their fathers﴾, and the paternal uncles have entered into the category of "fathers", and Allah, Exalted is He, has named the uncle a "father" in the Qur'an, saying, Exalted is He, relating from the tribes (al-Asbat) that they said to Ya'qub: ﴿We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim and Isma'il and Ishaq﴾, and Isma'il was the paternal uncle of Ya'qub.

As for His saying: ﴿nor their women﴾, there are two opinions concerning it. The first: that what is meant by "their women" is the Muslim women. According to this opinion, it was not permissible for Jewish and Christian women to enter upon them. The second opinion: that His saying ﴿nor their women﴾ is general, covering both Muslim and non-Muslim women. According to this opinion, He said ﴿nor their women﴾ only because they are of their kind (ajnas). According to the first opinion, He said ﴿nor their women﴾ (with the form nisa'ihinna) because their women are the Muslim women and not the non-Muslim women.

As for His saying: ﴿nor what their right hands possess﴾, there are two opinions concerning it. The first: that "what their right hands possess" refers to the female slaves (al-ima'). Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: "Let not this saying of His, ﴿nor what their right hands possess﴾, deceive you; it means only the female slaves, not the male slaves."

The second opinion: that what is meant by it is both the male slaves and the female slaves.

There has been disagreement as to up to what point male slaves are permitted to look at them, according to this opinion. One of the two opinions is that it is permissible for them to look at what is permissible for mahram relatives to look at.

The other opinion is that it is permissible to look at what usually shows of the face, the hands, and the feet, and it is not permissible to look at anything beyond that. This is the more cautious position.

As for His saying: ﴿And fear Allah﴾, this is an address to the wives of the Prophet, so that they do not go out uncovered and do not unveil themselves.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾, meaning: Witnessing (shahidan).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 56:

And the words of Allah Most High: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾. The ṣalāt (prayer, blessing) from Allah means mercy and forgiveness, while the ṣalāt of the angels and the believers means supplication (du'ā').

Thaʿlab said: the saying of the one who says, "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad," means: increase him in blessing and mercy. The origin of ṣalāt in the language is supplication, and we have explained this before. It has been established from the Prophet that he said: ((Whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah sends blessings upon him ten times)).

It is also mentioned in some reports: ((When Jibrīl (peace be upon him) descended with this, the Messenger of Allah prostrated in gratitude)).

It has been established by the narration of Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have learned how to greet you with peace, so how should we send blessings upon you?" He said: ((Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrāhīm and upon the family of Ibrāhīm; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious)).

And from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: When you send blessings upon the Messenger of Allah, then make your blessings upon him good, for perhaps they are presented to him. They said to him: "Teach us." He said: Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Your Prophet, the leader of the messengers, the imam of the God-fearing, the seal of the prophets, the imam of goodness, the leader of goodness, and the messenger of mercy. O Allah, raise him to the praiseworthy station which the first and the last will envy him for.

﴿Those who harm Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment﴾, and the last part [of the verse].

Al-Aṣmaʿī narrated: I heard al-Mahdī, who is Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr, on the pulpit of Basra saying: Indeed Allah Most High has commanded you with a matter in which He began with Himself, and then joined His angels to Himself, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace﴾.

As for greeting the Messenger with peace, it is that you say: "Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings." This applies to the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, and it was the Sunnah for them to address the Messenger in this manner. As for the rest of the believers, they say in the tashahhud what is well known.

Some scholars have mentioned that one says in the tashahhud: "Peace be upon the Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings," and does not say "upon you."

The correct view is what we have explained. Outside the prayer, one says: "Peace be upon the Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings."

This verse is used as evidence for the obligation of sending blessings upon the Prophet when one mentions him in prayer, according to the position of al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him). The reasoning is: Allah Most High has commanded us to send blessings upon the Prophet, and the most fitting place for the obligation of blessings is the prayer itself. Therefore it is obligatory to send blessings upon the Messenger of Allah within the prayer.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 57:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who abuse Allah and His Messenger﴾. It has been established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Allah, exalted is He, says: My servant reviles Me, and it is not fitting for him to revile Me; and My servant denies Me, and it is not fitting for him to deny Me. As for his reviling Me, it is that he claims that I have taken a son. As for his denying Me, it is that he claims that I will not restore My creation, whereas I am the Originator, the Restorer."

Some of them said: ﴿Indeed, those who abuse Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: the friends of Allah.

The more correct of the two sayings is that His saying ﴿abuse Allah﴾ is figurative (majaz). As for in its literal reality (haqiqah), no harm reaches Him from anyone.

And His saying: ﴿Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter﴾ means: He has banished them and removed them far from His mercy.

And His saying: ﴿And He has prepared for them a humiliating punishment﴾ means: He will humiliate and disgrace them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 58:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women without their having earned it﴾ means: they fall upon them (yaqa'una fihim) and find fault with them, without any offense having been committed by them that had reached them beforehand.

Muqatil mentioned here that the verse was revealed concerning a people who used to harm ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Kalbi mentioned that the verse was revealed concerning a group of the hypocrites (munafiqin) who used to walk along the road and make suggestive gestures (yaghmizun) at women.

As for His saying: ﴿then they have born a slander and a manifest sin﴾, its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 59:

The words of the Most High: ﴿O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their outer garments (jalabib) close around them.﴾ The commentators mention that Madinah had cramped dwellings, and women would go out at night into the open spaces (al-bawar) to attend to their needs. Some of the hypocrites and wicked men would lie in wait for them and accost them. If a woman was chaste, she would cry out and they would leave her alone; but if she was not chaste, they would give her something and have intercourse with her.

In another narration: they used to accost the female slaves (imaa') and did not accost the free women (hara'ir), so God Most High revealed this verse.

As for His words ﴿that they should draw their outer garments close around them﴾, meaning: they should wrap themselves in the jalabib. The jilbab is the rida' (wrapper), which is the sheet a woman wraps herself in over the dir' (shift) and the khimar (headcover).

Ubaydah al-Salmani said: the woman covers herself with her jilbab, concealing her head, her face and her whole body except one of her eyes.

It is related that when God Most High revealed this verse, the women of the Ansar took black woolen cloaks (akisah sawda'), wrapped themselves in them, and went out, as if their heads were ravens (al-ghirban).

As for His words ﴿That is more suitable that they will be known and not be harmed﴾, meaning: that they will be known to be free women, ﴿so that they will not be harmed﴾, meaning: that no one will molest them.

As for His words ﴿And God is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾, we have already explained this earlier.

When Umar (radiya Allahu anhu) saw a slave woman who had veiled herself and wrapped herself in a jilbab, he would strike her with his whip (al-durrah) and say: "Do you imitate the free women?"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 33, verse 60:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease do not cease﴾, i.e., the desire for fornication (zina).

And His saying: ﴿and the agitators in al-Madinah﴾. A group of the hypocrites used to spread many rumours (al-arajif). Whenever a detachment (sariyyah) or a raiding party (ghaziyah) went out, they would say: "They have been defeated and killed," and they would create such things among the Muslims, so that their hearts would be weakened and they would be grieved.

And His saying: ﴿We will surely set you over them﴾, i.e., We will give you authority over them and impel you to kill them.

In some exegeses it is mentioned that a group of the hypocrites intended to openly display disbelief, so God, may He be exalted, commanded His Messenger to kill them if they displayed it.

Al-Suddi said: whoever pursues a woman on a road and overpowers her is to be killed, whether he is married (muhsan) or not, on the basis of this verse.

And His saying: ﴿Then they will not be your neighbours therein﴾, i.e., in al-Madinah.

And His saying: ﴿except for a little﴾, i.e., except for a short time.

The Exalted said: ﴿Cursed﴾. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl).

And His saying: ﴿Wherever they are found﴾ means: wherever they are encountered and come upon.

And His saying: ﴿They shall be seized and slain, a fierce slaying﴾. As for His saying "qatalū taqtīlā" (they were slain with a fierce slaying), al-Suddī said: (مَا قَالَ)

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿The way of Allah with those who passed away before, and you will never find any change in the way of Allah﴾ (sunnat Allah, "the way of Allah," meaning His established practice and custom), and those who acted in the same manner as this act.

And His words: ﴿and you will never find any change in the way of Allah﴾, i.e., alteration.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 63:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The people ask you about the Hour﴾, i.e., when its establishment (qiyam) will be.

And His saying: ﴿Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah"﴾, i.e., the knowledge of its establishment is with Allah.

And His saying: ﴿And what will make you know?﴾, i.e., what will inform you? That is, you do not know the time of its establishment.

And His saying: ﴿Perhaps the Hour is near﴾, i.e., nearby.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 64:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers﴾, meaning: He has removed them far from mercy and driven them away from all good.

And His words: ﴿and has prepared for them a blaze﴾, meaning: a fire kindled and blazing.

And His saying: ﴿abiding therein forever﴾ has already been explained.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿they will find no protector or helper﴾

On the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire: meaning, they will be dragged on their faces in the Fire.

And His saying: ﴿They will say, "Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger."﴾ That is, "the Messenger." Mentioning "the Messenger" (al-Rasula) is for the sake of matching the endings of the verses (ru'us al-ayat), as we explained earlier.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (*Tafsir al-Qur'an*) on Surah 33, verse 67:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will say, "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our elders"﴾. It is also recited as "سَادَاتنَا" (*sādātanā*, the plural of *sayyid*, "master"). His saying, ﴿and our elders﴾, refers to the nobles and the leaders of the people.

His saying: ﴿and they misled us from the way﴾. That is, "al-sabīl" (the way), and its meaning is: they turned us away from the path of truth.

"His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment from the Fire﴾ means: punish them with twice the punishment of others. It is also said: punish them with the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, and the first is more preferable.

And His saying: ﴿and curse them with a great curse﴾ means: again and again, repeatedly. It is also read as "kathiran" with the letter thā' (ث), and the meaning is one and the same."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 69:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who abused Moses⦆. Its meaning: Do not harm Muhammad, lest you become like those who harmed Moses. Regarding what the Messenger was harmed with, there are two opinions. The first: they harmed him concerning the matter of Zayd ibn Harithah and his marriage to Zaynab.

The second: it is reported that he distributed a share of booty, and a man stood up and said: "Be just, for you have not been just." The Prophet said: "May God have mercy on Moses; he was harmed with more than this, and he was patient."

As for what Moses was harmed with, there are two opinions. The first, and most of the people of tafsir hold to it, is what Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, reported: that the Prophet said: "Moses was a modest man, very shy, and he would not bathe except alone. The Children of Israel used to bathe naked, looking at one another's private parts. They said: 'Moses does not bathe except alone because there is a defect in him.' And they said: 'He has a swollen testicle.' So Moses bathed once and placed his garment upon a rock, and the rock ran off with his garment. Moses took his staff and began saying: 'My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!' until he passed by a group of the Children of Israel, and they looked at him and saw no fault in him. The rock stopped, and he began striking it with the staff."

Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God said: "And it is as if I see the rock's marks from the impact of his striking it, four or five times." The report is in the two Sahihs.

In the report: "God, may He be exalted, sent down concerning this His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who abused Moses⦆, to the end of the verse."

In some narrations: the rock said to him: "O Moses, you did not strike me; I am only a servant under command."

The second opinion regarding the verse: it is reported from Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Aaron and Moses ascended the mountain, and Aaron died, and Moses came down alone. The Children of Israel said to him: "You killed Aaron, and he was gentler toward us than you and more beloved to us." So God sent the angels until they carried Aaron dead to them, and they spoke of his death until the Children of Israel heard it. Then the angels carried Aaron and buried him, and no one knew the place of his grave except the vulture. So God made it deaf and mute.

His saying: ﴿So God cleared him of what they said⦆, that is: God purified him from what they said.

His saying: ﴿And he was honorable (wajih) in the sight of God⦆, that is: by His speaking to him. Wajih in the language means one who has standing (jah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 70:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, fear God and speak words of directness﴾. That is: correct speech. It is also said: truthful speech.

It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas that it is the statement "There is no god but God" (lā ilāha illā Allāh). Some of them said: sadīdan means upright (mustaqīman). It is said: sadded, meaning: be upright (istaqim). Zuhayr said:

(So I said to him: "Be upright, and watch his path, / and what he is occupied with does not divert him from my counsel.")

That is: from my counsel. Some of them said: qawlan sadīdan means speech whose inner meaning agrees with its outer meaning.

And His saying: ﴿He will set right your deeds for you﴾, meaning: He will purify your deeds for you. It was also said: "He will set right your deeds for you" means: He will accept the good deeds from you.

And His saying: ﴿and forgive you your sins﴾, meaning: He will cover them up and pardon them.

And His saying: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment﴾, meaning: he has gained all good.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 72:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "The trust (al-amanah) is the obligatory duties (al-fara'id)." Al-Dahhak said: "Obedience (al-ta'ah)." It is reported from Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi: "What He commanded and what He forbade." Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: "The trust here is the guarding of the private parts (hifz al-farj)."

The most preferred of these statements is what we have mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas, and the statements of al-Dahhak and Abu al-'Aliyah are close to it. In some tafsir works it is said: "The first thing God Most High created of the son of Adam was his private part, and He entrusted it to him, and said: 'If you guard it, I will guard you.'"

It is reported from Abu Hamzah al-Sukkari that he said: "I know of myself that I would discharge the trust even with a hundred thousand dinars, and a hundred thousand dinars, and a hundred thousand dinars, until the breath ends. And if a woman stayed with me and I were entrusted with her, I would fear that I would not be safe from her."

It is reported from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Among the trust is the performance of the prayer, the giving of zakat, the fasting of Ramadan, the pilgrimage to the House, truthfulness in speech, the payment of debts, and justice in measures and weights." He said: "And more severe than all of this are the deposits." This statement is close to the statement of Ibn 'Abbas.

﴿...upon the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it; and man bore it. Indeed, he was ever wrongdoing and ignorant.﴾

The scholars said: "The trust is the pivot of faith. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'There is no faith for one who has no trustworthiness.'"

Among trustworthiness is that the inner state conforms to the outer state; so whoever does an action that contradicts his belief has betrayed God and His Messenger. God Most High has said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not betray God and the Messenger, or betray your trusts﴾. It was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir, who had placed his finger upon his throat, indicating to the Banu al-Nadir that if they came down, it would be slaughter. This has been explained previously.

As for His saying: ﴿upon the heavens and the earth and the mountains﴾, there are statements concerning it:

The first, which is the statement of most of the early generation, and is related from Ibn 'Abbas and a group of the Successors, is that God Most High presented His commands to the heavens, the earth and the mountains as an offer of choice, not an offer of obligation, and said to them: "Will you bear this trust with what is in it?" They said: "And what is in it?" He said: "If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you disobey, you will be punished." They said: "We will not bear the trust, and we do not desire reward or punishment." Then it was offered to Adam, and he bore it with what is in it. In some tafsir works it is said that he said: "Between my ear and my shoulder."

Ibn Juraj said: It was offered to the sky, and it said: "O Lord, You created me and made me a protected roof, and You set the sun, the moon and the stars moving in me, and I have no strength to bear the trust." Then it was offered to the earth, and it said: "O Lord, You created me and made me an outspread carpet, and You set rivers flowing in me, and You caused trees to grow in me, and I have no strength to bear the trust." He mentioned something similar concerning the mountains. And Adam and his offspring bore it. It is reported from Mujahid that he said: "The heavens, the earth and the mountains refused to bear the trust, and Adam bore it; and what was between his bearing it and his betrayal of it, and his expulsion from the Garden, was only the time between the noon prayer and the afternoon prayer."

Al-Naqqash related with his chain from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "The trust was likened to a rock laid down, and the heavens, the earth and the mountains were summoned to it, but they did not approach it, and said: 'We cannot bear it.' Adam came, without being called, and moved the rock, and said: 'Had I been commanded to bear it.' They said to him: 'Bear it.' So he bore it up to his knees, then set it down and said: 'By God, if I wished to increase, I would have increased.' They said: 'Bear it,' so he bore it up to his loins, then set it down and said: 'By God, if I wished to increase, I would have increased.' They said: 'Bear it,' so he bore it until it was placed on his shoulder, and he wanted to set it down, but God Most High said: 'Stay where you are,' and so it is upon your neck and the necks of your offspring until the Day of Resurrection."

If someone says: "How could it be offered to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, when they do not understand anything?" We say: "We have already explained the answer to such questions before." Some scholars said: "It is possible that God Most High created in them intellect and discernment at the time the trust was offered to them, until they understood the address and answered with what they answered."

As for His saying: ﴿but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it﴾, that means: they did not accept bearing the trust and feared it.

His saying: ﴿and man bore it﴾ means: Adam, peace be upon him.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, he was ever wrongdoing and ignorant﴾. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Wrongdoing to himself, ignorant of his Lord." This is related by Abu al-Husayn ibn Faris. The second statement: "Wrongdoing to himself by eating from the tree, ignorant of the outcome of his affair."

It is reported from a group of scholars that the intended meaning of "wrongdoing and ignorant" is the hypocrite and the polytheist. This has been related from al-Hasan in one narration.

The second statement regarding the basis of the verse is that what is intended by the offering to the heavens, the earth and the mountains is the offering to the people of the heavens, the people of the earth and the people of the mountains, and it is like His saying: ﴿and ask the town﴾, meaning: the people of the town.

The third statement was mentioned by al-Zajjaj and others among the scholars of meanings, who said: God Most High entrusted Adam and his offspring with something, and entrusted the heavens, the earth and the mountains with something. As for the trust regarding the children of Adam, it is known; and as for the trust regarding the heavens, the earth and the mountains, it means submission and obedience. God Most High said: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: "Come willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly."﴾

It is related that prostration was attributed to the heavens, the earth, the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees and the animals, and He mentioned concerning stones His saying: ﴿And indeed, among them is that which descends out of fear of God.﴾

His saying: ﴿but they refused to bear it﴾ means: they refused to discharge the trust concerning it. It is said: "So-and-so did not bear the trust," meaning he did not betray in it.

His saying: ﴿and were apprehensive of it﴾ means: they discharged the trust out of fear of it.

His saying: ﴿and man bore it﴾ means: he betrayed it and sinned; it is said: "So-and-so bore the trust," meaning he sinned in it by betrayal. God Most High said: ﴿And they will surely bear their burdens and burdens along with their burdens﴾. As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, he was ever wrongdoing and ignorant﴾, it has been explained. Al-Azhari said: "Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj has excelled and done well in this statement and was praised for it, and the statement of the early generation is what we have explained before."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 73:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿That Allah may punish the hypocrites, men and women﴾. The lam here is the lam of purpose (lam kay), and its meaning is: so that Allah may punish the hypocrites, men and women, and the polytheists, men and women, meaning when they betray (the trust).

And His words: ﴿And Allah turns in mercy toward the believers, men and women﴾, meaning: He guides them and has mercy on them when they fulfill the trust.

It is related from Ibn Qutaybah that he said: its meaning is: that He may expose the hypocrites, men and women, and the polytheists, men and women, and punish them for betraying the trusts, and that He may manifest the believers, men and women, through their fulfilling of the trust.

And His words: ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾, the meaning of which is clear.
